2608.23393.abstract: KellyBoost is a single multi-output XGBoost model whose softmax output is the portfolio: with y the vector of per-asset holding-period returns, the training loss is - log(1 + w y), the negative log growth rate, so the fitted model is the growth-optimal (Kelly) allocation conditioned on the features. The objective is exact rather than a surrogate: we derive the gradient, the analytic diagonal Hessian and the full Hessian in closed form, verify them by finite differences, and ship a dependency-free reference engine.

2608.23416.abstract: Systematic trading rests on one article of faith: that regularities found in the past persist. We state it as a time-invariant mechanism driven by an unobserved latent state, and show that it leaves a researcher five constants to declare --- the recurrence bound $Lambda$ at a block length $b$, the invariance defect $epsilon_0$ of the representation it is declared of, the coherence times $ell_i$ of the state's coordinates, the signal ceiling $rho$ and the fraction $kappa$ of it contingent on the regime --- after which the architecture of a correct quantitative investment system is nearly forced.

2608.23416.title: The Axiomatic Trader: Latent Regularity, Information Budgets, and the Canonical Form of a Quantitative Investment System

2608.23576.abstract: We characterise minimum-distortion wealth taxation under two contrasting normative criteria within a Fokker-Planck framework on log-wealth: the JKO free-energy gap, an information-theoretic measure aligned with the Mirrleesian decision-distortion tradition, and the squared 2-Wasserstein distance from the no-tax distribution at horizon $T$, a transport-geometric measure aligned with the Saez-Zucman distributional-compression tradition. Restricting to the neutrality-preserving (C1)-(C3) schedule class of a companion paper (Froseth 2026), both optima admit closed forms in the two-dimensional design plane parametrised by the corporate-dividend retention $k = (1-τ_c)(1-τ_d)$ and the proportional wealth-tax rate $τ_w$. The JKO optimum partitions the regime axis into three phases as a function of the dimensionless ratio $ρ= Σ_0 m_0/σ^2$, with $m_0 = μ- σ^2/2$ the geometric mean log-return: a pure wealth-tax phase at low $ρ$, a mixed-instrument phase at intermediate $ρ$, and a pure flow-tax phase at high $ρ$. The $W_2$ optimum, by contrast, is degenerate in this calibration: it pins to the pure flow-tax corner across the whole regime axis. The criterion contrast admits an economically meaningful reading via a bluntness index $B(m_0) = b/(a m_0)$ that measures the wealth-tax channel's mean-displacement-per-revenue overshoot relative to the flow-tax channel; JKO weights $B$ linearly, $W_2$ weights it quadratically, and the two normative traditions correspond to this difference in weighting. Norwegian-flavoured calibrations sit inside the JKO mixed-instrument phase under stock-heavy portfolio volatility but move into the pure flow-tax phase under the realised effective volatility of typical real-estate-heavy households.

2608.23576.title: Minimum-Distortion Wealth Taxation, I: Information-Theoretic versus Transport-Geometric Optimality on the Proportional Class

2608.24449.abstract: We show that the key optimization results of the classical Markowitz portfolio selection theory, originally formulated for variance as the risk measure, remain available in explicit closed form under a broader class of strictly convex quadratic risk measures. The proposed framework replaces the covariance matrix with an arbitrary symmetric positive definite matrix and allows additional linear and constant terms, thereby containing various models arising in transaction cost optimization, benchmark relative optimization, covariance regularization, and factor models. Closed-form formulas are obtained for the efficient frontier, the global minimum risk portfolio, the maximum Sharpe ratio portfolio, the Capital Market Curve, the tangency portfolio, and the maximum utility portfolio. In contrast to the classical Markowitz model, the tangency portfolio does not coincide with the maximum Sharpe ratio portfolio, revealing a new geometric phenomenon. A numerical example confirms the derived formulas.

2608.24449.title: Generalizing Markowitz Portfolio Optimization by a Quadratic Risk Measure

2608.26106.abstract: We study statistical predictability in daily U.S. equity prices using only information available at the market open. Using SPY from February 1, 1993 through March 15, 2024, we benchmark XGBoost against Random Forest, LightGBM, Logistic Regression, and naive baselines under expanding-window walk-forward validation. After observing the current day's opening price and two lagged target-specific prices, the task is to predict whether the same day's close will be above or below the previous day's close. On the last 800 trading days, Logistic Regression attains the highest close-direction accuracy (71.09%), Random Forest reaches 61.20%, and XGBoost reaches 58.45% with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [54.94%, 62.08]. For XGBoost, close-direction accuracy rises to 72.7% when the predicted move exceeds 1%, but the usable sample falls to 154 observations. We also report Diebold-Mariano and McNemar tests, regime-specific results, SHAP feature importance, and an auxiliary 541-equity screen. The evidence supports a narrow statistical-finance conclusion: simple daily equity features contain detectable same-day directional information, but the result should be interpreted with careful sample-size accounting and limited economic claims.

2608.26106.title: A Statistical-Finance Benchmark for Same-Day Directional Stock Prediction: Walk-Forward Evidence from SPY

2608.26115.abstract: We re-estimate canonical option-implied predictability evidence using a unified 2015--2026 panel of 12.36 million U.S. equity firm-day observations across 10,026 underlyings. We split the sample into three regimes: late-post-crisis low volatility (2015--2019), high-volatility transition (2020--2022), and AI/mega-cap concentration (2023--2026). The Xing et al. (2010) smirk--return relationship weakens steadily: the next-month univariate smirk coefficient falls from $-0.023$ $(t=-5.5)$ in 2015--2019 to an insignificant $-0.006$ $(t=-1.5)$ in 2023--2026, and turns positive at the three-month horizon $(+0.016,\ t=+2.1)$. In joint specifications with all six canonical signals, the smirk is insignificant throughout and again changes sign in the latest regime. By contrast, the Cremers--Weinbaum IV spread and a Bakshi et al. (2003)-style risk-neutral skewness measure remain significant across regimes and specifications. A boosted-tree benchmark using IV-surface, trading-activity, Greeks, and liquidity features outperforms linear models for next-month return prediction only in the AI/mega-cap regime, with $R^2_{\mathrm{OOS}}=+1.29%$ versus $+0.07%$. Permutation importance identifies different leading predictors by regime, and no canonical hand-engineered signal enters the top five. For firm-level five-day crash classification, AUC is highest in calm markets $(0.706,\ \text{XGBoost})$ and lowest during the high-volatility transition $(0.561)$. Overall, option-implied predictability is real but regime-dependent, and the post-2023 AI/mega-cap period differs sharply from the pre-COVID setting in which the canonical results were established.

2608.26115.title: Option-Implied Signals and Crash Risk: Predictability and Machine-Learning Evidence from U.S. Equity Options

2608.26122.abstract: This article examines various methods of constructingmultidimensional probabilistic forecasts of electricity prices. Building on the Multiple Split (MS) method, it incorporates forecast averaging across estimation windows of different lengths and compares its performance with that of other, well-established methods. The research demonstrates that the ensemble representation of the price distribution is particularly useful in battery energy storage system (BESS) management. It enables the direct construction of probabilistic forecasts of daily profits. These forecasts can be used to determine optimal charging and discharging hours, as well as to support risk management decisions. The methods are evaluated using data from the German and Spanish day-ahead electricity markets from 2021-2024. The results indicate that theMS method with averaging (MS-ave) generally outperforms the other considered approaches in terms of Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP), the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) and the Energy Score (ES). Moreover, it is superior in supporting BESS trading strategies, particularly in case of non-zero operational costs.

2608.26122.title: From electricity prices to profits: multidimensional probabilistic forecasting for BESS trading

2608.26127.abstract: Accurate forecasting of realized volatility ($RV$) is crucial for risk management and derivatives pricing. Although the implied volatility ($IV$) surface offers rich informational content, prevailing methods that treat it as a static image fail to capture its inherent dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Finance-Aware Graph Spatio-Temporal Network (FA-GSTN), a novel architecture that reframes $RV$ forecasting as modeling the evolution of a structured financial object. FA-GSTN builds a spatio-temporal graph sequence from the $IV$ surface, where nodes correspond to grid points and edges encode adaptive spatial (intra-day) and explicit temporal (inter-day) dependencies. The model incorporates domain knowledge through finance-aware node features (e.g., option Greeks) and tackles high-frequency noise via a multi-scale temporal smoothing gate coupled with an adaptive robust loss function. Comprehensive evaluations on a large-scale equity options dataset show that FA-GSTN sets a new state of the art, delivering superior predictive accuracy ($R^2$ up to 0.473). It also demonstrates remarkable data efficiency, substantially outperforming strong Vision Transformer baselines when trained on only one year of data ($R^2$: 0.372 vs. 0.315). Furthermore, the model exhibits enhanced robustness during periods of market stress, such as 2020--2021. Ablation studies confirm the vital roles of the spatio-temporal graph structure, finance-aware components, and integrated noise-handling modules. Our work underscores the substantial benefits of explicitly modeling temporal dynamics and infusing financial inductive biases for accurate and robust volatility forecasting.

2608.26127.title: Graph-Based Modeling of Financial Volatility Dynamics

2608.26128.abstract: This thesis analyzes the collective dynamics of the S&P 500 from an econophysics perspective, treating the financial market as a complex system. Using daily logarithmic returns of 430 companies, time-dependent Pearson correlation matrices are constructed over sliding windows and their spectral structure is studied through the leading eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Market States (MS) are identified by applying k-Means clustering to several spectral quantities: the largest eigenvalue (interpreted as the State of the Market), the squared entries of the dominant eigenvector (read as a relative participation of each stock), and truncated matrix reconstructions C^l built from the l largest eigenpairs and normalized to retain a correlation-matrix interpretation. The stability of the resulting clusters is assessed, transition matrices and their stationary vectors are computed, and the inverse participation ratio is used to quantify how participation spreads across assets. The COVID-19 episode emerges as an atypical state in the full correlation matrices; reconstructing it requires more than one principal component, and the C^2 and C^3 constructions reproduce it, particularly for window length q=40 and k=5. During crisis periods the relative participation distributes over a larger number of assets, while the 2017-2018 interval contributes to the dynamics without appearing as an isolated regime. The analysis is descriptive rather than predictive, and provides conceptual and methodological tools relevant to portfolio design and trading strategies, with natural extensions to other international exchanges.

2608.26128.title: Analysis of the Principal Components of Correlation Matrices of S&P 500 Financial Data from an Econophysics Perspective

2608.26158.abstract: This paper provides a controlled comparison of six information bar types (dollar, volume, volatility, range, Renko, and hybrid bars) constructed from both raw Binance aggTrade tick data and one-minute OHLCV bars for the BTCUSDT USDT-margined perpetual futures market over a six-year period spanning January 2020 to December 2025, and evaluated against fixed-interval time-bar baselines. Both pipelines share a common adaptive EMA calibration framework; the tick pipeline additionally uses strictly tick-native activity signals, isolating data resolution as the sole experimental variable. Results across eight statistical quality criteria reveal that the tick advantage is bar-type-specific and most pronounced in bar types whose activity signals are most sensitive to intra-minute price dynamics: tick Renko bars achieve the smallest random-walk deviation recorded ($|\mathrm{VR}(4){-}1| = 0.020$, lag-1 autocorrelation $= 0.002$), and tick volatility bars reduce serial dependence by 69\% relative to the minute baseline ($|\mathrm{VR}(4){-}1|: 0.028$ versus $0.089$). In the multi-regime six-year sample, normality improvements are regime-dependent and secondary: the extreme market events of 2020--2022 inflate fat tails across all bar types, and Ljung-Box independence is rejected for all series at the sample sizes studied. A matched-frequency robustness analysis shows that the apparent tick underperformance on distributional criteria is largely a sampling-frequency artefact: when tick series are coarsened to the minute pipeline's bar count, frequency-matched tick dollar bars lead on all six criteria and matched tick volatility bars attain LB $p = 0.51$, recovering serial independence that the raw oversampled series rejects.

2608.26158.title: A Frequency-Controlled Comparison of Tick- and Minute-Based Information Bars for Cryptocurrency Markets

2608.26174.abstract: Bitcoin's future fluctuations are a substantial concern for investments and risk management. Investors and financial institutions require accurate forecasts of these price movements to hedge and optimize portfolios. This study aims to answer the question of whether Bitcoin's price will rise beyond 5% within the next 7 days by utilizing on-chain, market, and sentiment data from February 2018 to December 2025. The proposed model consists of a multi-scale temporal convolutional network with InceptionTCN blocks, CNN channel attention, adaptive average pooling, and a pairwise ranking loss. Dilated convolutions with bottleneck and fusion layers are employed to efficiently capture features over horizons from 1 to 4 days. Given the class imbalance in the dataset, AUC is used instead of accuracy and other classification metrics to reflect the model's performance better. Subsequently, a profit-optimized decision threshold is also applied to align model selection with financial objectives. The proposed model is compared with 5 other baselines: ImprovedTCN_GRU, LSTM, TCN, XGBoost, and Random Forest. Results indicate that the proposed model achieved an AUC of 0.6316 and a profit of 1.703, outperforming all baseline models. Using a novel deep learning model would assist investors in making better financial decisions.

2608.26174.title: Forecasting Economically Significant Bitcoin Moves: A Multi-Scale TCN with Profit-Optimized Thresholds

2608.27076.abstract: Algorithmic trading now represents a market exceeding $20 billion, where even marginal gains in signal robustness can translate into economically significant returns. Existing evaluations of equity prediction models do not explicitly target regime robustness during hyperparameter selection. Five model classes are trained on daily observations from approximately 300 large-cap US equities over eleven years, with Bayesian optimisation configured to target trading performance across three statistically different market regimes. Regime-robust hyperparameter selection is associated with out-of-sample generalisation, as signal precision remains above the random baseline across all four quarters of the test period, and portfolio performance slowly degrades under simulated input noise before collapsing beyond a defined threshold. No individual tabular deep learning architecture outperforms gradient-boosted trees, but combining XGBoost and TabNet using rank aggregation produces a Hybrid ensemble with an annualised return of 51.26%, a Sharpe ratio of 2.44, and a statistically significant CAPM alpha of 0.423 (p = 0.011). A near-zero beta indicates this outperformance is driven by stock selection, not market exposure. Alternative data plays a secondary role once technical and fundamental features are accounted for, as well as contributing more strongly on the short side than the long, and varies by model class. An interactive application makes these results explorable in real time, with live data integration the remaining step toward practical deployment.

2608.27076.title: Tabular Deep Learning for Algorithmic Trading: Cross-Regime Bayesian Optimisation for Equity Signal Generation

2608.27734.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to discover trading strategies, and much of the resulting literature shares a methodological weakness: many candidate strategies are generated, the best is reported, and neither look-ahead bias nor the intensity of the search behind the reported result is corrected for. We present a strategy-discovery system that makes both corrections structural rather than procedural. First, the agent can only act through registry-validated tools whose feature space excludes look-ahead by construction; we show that this guardrail is not redundant with statistical correction: a deliberately leaky oracle posting a Sharpe ratio of 35 survives Deflated Sharpe and probability-of-backtest-overfitting testing completely. Second, the system records every strategy evaluation its search performs and deflates all reported performance by that trial count, tracing how the best in-sample Sharpe ratio climbs with each trial while the deflation threshold, driven by the agent's own search, climbs faster. Across a 453-stock point-in-time US equity universe and a 39-ETF multi-asset universe with realistic transaction, impact, and borrow costs, honest evaluation certifies passive benchmarks (out-of-sample confidence intervals excluding zero), rejects every LLM-discovered strategy (across two frontier models, search budgets up to one hundred candidates, and five repeated runs), catching selection luck, predicted rank degradation, and out-of-sample collapse through complementary instruments, and evaluates a human trader's production rule system under identical instruments. The framework formalizes why pre-registered hypotheses earn lower evidential bars than brute search, and quantifies the sample sizes that credible certification of moderate edges actually requires.

2608.27734.title: What survives honest evaluation? Leakage-safe, search-aware assessment of LLM-driven trading strategy discovery

2608.28399.abstract: In financial markets, a sequential policy that reacts systematically to price movements may become predictable to other market participants. This paper studies whether large language model (LLM) agents exhibit such directional structure through RetailAgent, an experimental framework in which an LLM observes anonymized intraday equity price histories and permitted state, then repeatedly chooses long (hold the stock) or flat (stay out) before the subsequent interval return is revealed. We compare returns during long and flat intervals along the same stock's intraday path after removing the overall fraction of long decisions. This exposure-matched measure reveals persistent negative timing across modality, horizon, state, and model family. Shuffling saved action sequences substantially attenuates the effect, showing that alignment between actions and subsequent returns drives the negative score. Feeding self-authored memories into decisions further increases policy persistence, while timing becomes more negative among stock-days on which the agent uses both actions. These results reveal stable, recoverable directional structure in sequential LLM financial decisions and a behavioral signal for studying how another participant could respond to a predictable policy.

ssrn-7346819.abstract: Investors price commercial property partly on how it looks, yet visual attributes rarely appear in the data used to study transaction pricing. Using satellite and street view imagery for 6,533 U.S. single-tenant net lease transactions from 2005 to 2020, we read each property's images two ways: as scores against attributes we name in advance, and as unlabeled statistical summaries. Together they close about 6.5 percent of the cap rate variation left unexplained by conventional property, market, lease, and time controls, and the named attributes account for most of it. The gain survives county fixed effects, public controls for walkability, demographics, urban form, and flood risk, and it improves out-of-sample forecasts. Because most of what imagery contributes can be stated in words, appraisal and underwriting can use it without sacrificing transparency.

ssrn-7355099.abstract: On August 10, 2026, Nvidia announced memoranda of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize over five hundred billion dollars of third-party capital through GPU-backed financing platforms. This paper argues that the structure introduces a category of risk that existing asset-backed securitisation theory does not formally address. I identify three conditions shared with the mortgage-backed securities market before 2008: correlated collateral values, unproven cash flow assumptions, and asymmetric incentives between originators and downstream debt holders. I then define two risk categories specific to technology asset-backed lending: Vendor-Circular Financing, which describes the structural conflict created when a manufacturer backstops credit facilities enabling purchases of its own products, and Innovation-Cycle Depreciation, which describes the systematic destruction of collateral value triggered by the vendor's own product roadmap. Secondary market data shows that H100 GPUs have lost approximately seventy-three percent of their 2023 value by mid-2026, providing preliminary empirical grounding for both risk categories.

ssrn-7355943.abstract: Financial technology has reshaped the way capital is raised, invested, traded, and supervised. Innovations in electronic trading, algorithmic execution, digital advisory services, and distributed infrastructure have altered the structure of capital markets and the delivery of investment management services, while introducing new categories of operational, technological, and regulatory risk. This research examines financial technology as it applies to investment management and capital market services. It considers the FinTech ecosystem and its participants, the digital transformation of primary and secondary markets, the risk management and cybersecurity implications of technology adoption, the governance and internal control frameworks required to oversee it, and the contribution of financial technology to financial inclusion. The study concludes with an assessment of the developments expected to shape investment management and capital market infrastructure over the coming decade.

ssrn-7355962.abstract: Financial markets increasingly depend upon sophisticated technological infrastructures that facilitate the efficient exchange of information, movement of funds, settlement of transactions, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity protection, and operational resilience. These foundational technologies serve as critical enablers of modern financial systems and support the stability, efficiency, and scalability of financial services globally. This research examines the technological infrastructure underlying contemporary financial markets, with particular emphasis on financial market infrastructures, payment systems, cloud computing, data management, digital identity systems, cybersecurity frameworks, regulatory technologies, operational resilience, and emerging digital architectures. The study analyzes the role of infrastructure in enabling financial innovation while maintaining security, reliability, and market integrity. Furthermore, the research explores future developments that are expected to transform the architecture of financial systems over the coming decades.

ssrn-7356059.abstract: The digitization of judicial systems has radically transformed intake and case processing channels through electronic filing (efiling) platforms. However, the effectiveness of this infrastructure is severely constrained by a structural gap: the lack of standardization and quality control in the stage prior to formal submission (pre-filing). This paper examines the operational and conceptual distinction between the technological capacity of the reception portal and the integrity of the documentary input. Through a dogmatic-procedural, technical, and comparative analysis, it demonstrates how preventable documentary inconsistencies generate procedural friction, correction queues, requests for evidence (RFEs), and institutional rework. Finally, it theorizes and proposes the Pre-Filing Procedural Integrity Framework (PIF) as a dimension of preventive procedural economy and a guarantee of functional access to justice.

ssrn-7356758.abstract: We document a large and robust pre-announcement drift in Japanese equity indices ahead of scheduled Bank of Japan (BOJ) monetary policy decisions: prices drift up steadily in the days before a meeting, peak immediately ahead of the decision, and do not continue afterward, earning an economically large and statistically significant excess return without elevated volatility. The drift is concentrated in meetings preceded by high ex-ante implied volatility. It is the Bank-of-Japan analog of the pre-FOMC drift of Lucca and Moench (2015), with a distinctive Japanese feature-variable announcement timing-that aids identification.

ssrn-7356939.abstract: The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) is usually discussed as a matter of supervisory detail: the rules for stablecoins, the requirements for service providers, and the perimeter of decentralised finance. This paper argues that MiCA's most consequential problems are structural, and that they lie at the intersection of regulatory law and private international law. It develops a single method: control as the criterion of responsibility and entitlement, coordinated across borders through conflict-of-laws connecting factors. From that method it derives a reform agenda. It proposes an objective directed-activity test for reverse solicitation, transposed from Pammer and Hotel Alpenhof; a general antiabuse rule for MiCA; a controller-of-last-resort attribution rule for decentralised finance; a functional property rule for tokens grounded in Article 114 TFEU; a crypto-specific presumption of the centre of main interests anchored in Eurofood and Interedil; and a free-standing conflict-of-laws Regulation for the proprietary aspects of tokens, with the effective locus of control over key-management infrastructure as the connecting factor for custody. It closes with a ten-principle framework for a transnational private law of digital-asset custody. The paper's contribution is to show that the perimeter, stablecoin, DeFi and private-law questions form one problem, and that control and private international law supply their common solution.

ssrn-7357138.abstract: In July 2026 the Dubai Financial Services Authority asked whether any regulatory barrier stands in the way of issuing tokenised fund units in the Dubai International Financial Centre. This paper argues that the barrier is legal rather than technological, and that the Authority has already described it without naming it. Section 8.7 of the Collective Investment Rules requires a fund manager to keep a register of unitholders. It attributes no legal effect to that register. The register is not conclusive evidence of title, or evidence of title, and no power of rectification accompanies it. The DIFC Digital Assets Law of 2024 provides that the person in control of a digital asset is presumed to hold the superior title. One legal order therefore supplies an answer and a silence, and the answer was drafted for native crypto assets rather than for fund units. The paper meets the objection that this tension is illusory. The DIFC statute admits only assets that exist independently of any person and of any legal system, and a fund unit is a right constituted by a legal system. The objection is well founded, and it does not rescue the position. It produces what this paper calls the constitutive paradox. Either the tokenised unit is a digital asset, and control governs by default; or it is not, and the token carries no proprietary protection at all under the law that issued it. The paper then identifies a second gap, which it calls the anchoring problem. Article 129 of the DIFC Law of Security refers the applicable law for security rights in digital assets, and in assets embodied in digital assets, to the laws of England and Wales. That provision reaches tokenised fund units used as collateral. It refers the question to a system that has not yet settled it. Outside the security context nothing governs title at all. The paper states the case for that referral before answering it and compares the DIFC with the Abu Dhabi Global Market. It proposes anchoring by designation, modelled on Principle 5 of the UNIDROIT Principles on Digital Assets and Private Law, and applies the same reasoning to collateral, custody and insolvency.

ssrn-7359658.abstract: We develop a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for analyzing Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) allocation in decentralized exchange (DEX) markets under Proposer-Builder Separation (PBS). The model follows the PBS block-production pipeline from uninformed DEX-user transactions to searcher bundle construction, builder block assembly, proposer block selection, and on-chain execution. Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) optimizes participant policies in this shared execution environment, and average approximate best-response (ABR) regret quantifies the residual unilateral gains found by a finite evaluation procedure that holds all other agents' policies fixed and retrains one agent at a time. In a two-pool, single-token-pair experimental instantiation, we compare a configuration with two back-running searchers against a mixed configuration with one sandwich searcher and one back-running searcher. This distinction matters because a back-running transaction is appended after observed order flow and does not change the amount of output tokens received by the original uninformed trader, whereas a sandwich attack places searcher transactions around a targeted victim swap and can reduce the amount of output tokens received by that trader. The results show that MEV-related cumulative rewards are allocated differently across these configurations. Searchers convert visible order flow into bundle profits, builders aggregate these bundles through block construction, and builder competition transfers part of the resulting value to the proposer through block bids. Permitting sandwich attacks lowers uninformed traders' cumulative rewards and increases reward asymmetry among searchers.

ssrn-7359662.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how citizenship is exercised. Decisions about welfare, mobility, work, knowledge and political communication increasingly depend on data and automated systems operating across territorial and legal boundaries. These systems also require energy, water, minerals, labour and land, revealing the physical limits of seemingly immaterial digitalisation. Established accounts of digital citizenship explain rights, participation, inclusion and people's capacity to act through data. They give less attention, however, to ecological costs, ownership of essential infrastructure and consequences that extend across places and generations. This chapter develops EcoTechnoPolitical Citizenship as a framework connecting these concerns. It defines citizenship as the practical capacity to claim digital rights, participate in collective decisions, shape technological infrastructure and accept ecological responsibilities according to each actor's power and contribution. The framework has four dimensions: the physical and ecological basis of digital systems; democratic control over infrastructure; meaningful citizen agency; and responsibility across territories, supply chains and generations. The chapter traces the development of digital citizenship towards automated public life and explains AI economics through data, computing capacity, finance, labour and public dependence. It then examines the digital-green transition, which seeks to align digitalisation with sustainability but often leaves technological growth outside enforceable ecological limits. Practical implications are developed for impact assessment, public digital infrastructure, data commons, territorial oversight, citizen participation and education. Particular attention is paid to unequal power among citizens, governments, firms and communities affected by infrastructure. EcoTechnoPolitical Citizenship ultimately provides an accessible conceptual map for governing AI-dependent societies democratically while respecting planetary limits.

ssrn-7363041.abstract: The Gravity paper claims a recovered growth rate—the arch—for an investor who holds a baseline allocation and exercises stored safety after damage. This paper tests that claim in simulation, discovers the structure underneath it, and proves what the simulation found. The arch is an exact long-run law. Under the bang-bang shortfall rule studied here, for baselines below the market the gap to the arch line is positive recurrent with a closed-form stationary law. The fraction of time spent at Kelly converges to (p^* = y_0/(2-y_0)), and mean log-growth converges to the arch. At the market seat, the stationary law disappears and the convergence becomes degenerate. At the 20- and 50-year horizons tested, the arch is kept by both the median and the dollar mean, but not yet by mean log-wealth: the remaining shortfall is a transient whose clock is computable. Against the natural skeptic—a static portfolio at twice the baseline, or at the best static seat for the same goal—the moving portfolio loses on growth and dispersion and wins on the one thing it was built for: the probability of keeping the line. It does so with less average exposure, and for a computable number of years: 67 at 30/70, 78 at 50/50, 91 at 70/30, and 122 at the market. The crossover boundary (T^*(y_0)) is exactly characterized—the static side in closed form and the moving side by an explicit Laplace transform—and evaluated numerically as a curve in years. What remains outside the theorem—which paths fall deep, and how deep, before the law asserts itself—is the price. The price is itself a finding: exact, at a price, over time, within limits.

ssrn-7363442.abstract: Attributing future systemic tail losses across assets remains dominated by exposures estimated asset by asset, market beta, downside beta and volatility, although drawdowns are precisely the episodes in which losses become collective and concentrate where shocks recirculate among tightly co-moving names. The quantities proposed here originate in our prior work on network fragility: the FSRI, a structural index for microbial co-occurrence networks in agricultural soils, and its financial descendant, the TSI, whose standalone version we falsified and reported. From that starting point we hypothesized that the same structural information could carry marginal value if localized to individual assets, extended with a response dimension, and handed to a flexible learner as features rather than composed by hand. The result is the Omega Block: five per-asset features computed from daily prices alone, two triadic quantities measured against a closed-form configuration null and three response quantities around scheduled FOMC announcements, among them Omega-R, a perturbation response normalized by each asset's own baseline drift, developed for this block. In pre-registered paired ablations with a same-width noise placebo, the block adds 1.3 to 3.4 points of out-of-fold R 2 to next-year tail-loss attribution over baselines that instantiate the public state of the art, up to 31 columns including sector, downside beta, co-moments, a conditional MES proxy, size, liquidity and balance-sheet fundamentals, replicated on two universes and two nearly disjoint periods (2012-2017, 2016-2025), while the placebo worsens the same model in every configuration. Because the baselines that decide adoption in practice are proprietary, the paper's verification is designed to travel to the data: an open acceptance harness reruns the entire protocol on any universe, baseline and event calendar, with a values-only mode and a cryptographic time-lock. The scope established by the evidence is cross-sectional attribution, not market timing.

ssrn-7363443.abstract: We survey 28 leading Swiss pension fund consultants and asset managers to understand the factors and their ranking driving institutional asset allocation decisions. The risk tolerance of pension fund boards, target returns, and risk-free rates emerge as the most influential factors, while traditional portfolio theory predictors such as expected returns, volatility or individual risk aversion show limited practical relevance. Finally, we find that individual risk aversion of beneficiaries plays a limited role. Our findings suggest that while institutional investors may overcome individual suboptimal asset allocation choices, they face distinct institutional frictions that also influence asset allocation decisions.

ssrn-7363482.abstract: Buying an asset immediately after a large single day decline is one of the oldest ideas in short horizon trading, and it is easy to make it look profitable. This paper applies one event definition and one testing protocol to two asset classes, four US equity indices over seventy six years and, in results carried over from an earlier stage of the same research program, twenty cryptocurrency perpetual futures, and finds that almost all of the apparent effect is an artifact of how the events are counted. Large declines arrive on the same few calendar dates across instruments, so an event study that treats each instrument day as an independent observation is counting one market wide shock many times. In a panel of twenty eight single names, 1,361 declines at or below seven percent are only 791 distinct dates, and the pooled t statistic of 6.76 falls to 1.68 when each date is counted once. Three further corrections matter and are usually skipped: the depth thresholds that define such events are nested rather than independent, so a strong tail leaks into every shallower cut; testing several depths requires a familywise correction; and a stationary block bootstrap with a block length that is a large fraction of the sample is badly anti conservative, which in our own first pass manufactured a p value two orders of magnitude too small. After all four corrections, exactly one result survives in equities. Index declines at or below seven percent, 50 events on 25 dates clustering into 10 episodes since 1950, are followed by a mean next session return of 3.08 percent, with a familywise p value of 0.006 and a bootstrap interval from 1.34 to 4.84 percent. It is not crash window drift: the next session returns 3.08 percent while each of the following nine averages 0.01 percent, below the unconditional daily mean. It is implementable, since 83 percent of the move occurs after the opening print. Everything shallower is indistinguishable from zero, and the corresponding single name effect is absent. In crypto perpetuals the same mechanism fails completely, with an edge net of market beta that is negative in every regime and every year of a six year sample. The economics are the final constraint: an account trading the surviving tail signal deploys 0.05 percent of its capital time and beats Treasury bills by 0.44 points a year, which is a real effect that cannot carry a portfolio.

ssrn-7364940.abstract: Blockchain technology has emerged as a transformative innovation with the potential to enhance transparency, security, and efficiency in banking operations. However, empirical evidence on its effect on transaction transparency within the context of Industry 4.0 remains limited. This study investigates the relationship between blockchain adoption and transaction transparency in the banking sector, with particular attention to implementation practices, transparency outcomes, and the challenges influencing adoption. A quantitative descriptive research design was employed using a structured questionnaire administered to 120 banking professionals drawn from commercial, microfinance, and central banks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression in SPSS, with the measurement instrument demonstrating good internal reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.858). The findings reveal a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between blockchain adoption and transaction transparency (r = 0.713, p < 0.001). Regression analysis further indicates that blockchain adoption explains 50.8% of the variance in transaction transparency (R² = 0.508), highlighting its substantial contribution to improving transparency within banking operations. Respondents identified enhanced auditability, fraud reduction, operational efficiency, and regulatory confidence as key benefits, while budget constraints, legacy system integration, regulatory uncertainty, and limited technical expertise were identified as major barriers to implementation. The study contributes to the growing literature on blockchain-enabled digital transformation by providing empirical evidence on the role of blockchain in enhancing transaction transparency within the Industry 4.0 paradigm. The findings offer practical insights for banking executives, policymakers, and regulators seeking to strengthen transparency, trust, and operational performance through blockchain adoption.

ssrn-7365578.abstract: When an AI system appears to generate equity alpha, five explanations compete with genuine skill: factor exposure, a weak benchmark, data leakage, model complexity, and an advantage a conventional system could replicate. We test all five on the same signal. Using the peer-reviewed replication of 212 published anomalies, language-model and agentic arms forecast which anomalies persist after their original samples end. The arms earn significant factor alpha-and none of it survives comparison with a passive portfolio of all published anomalies, which requires no model at all. Leakage does not explain the result: contamination made performance worse. The models' verbal mechanism judgements outperform their own numeric scores, but in-sample persistence absorbs them. A composite forecast scoring 0.400 owes 98.5% of that to a statistic we supplied. Apparent AI alpha here is a benchmarking artefact, not information.

ssrn-7365579.abstract: Investment banking, shadow banking, and high-frequency trading are among those manifestations of modern finance that evoke fascination and mistrust in equal measure. Drawing on the academic literature and on current data from international institutions (Financial Stability Board, ESMA, SEC, LSEG), this paper examines what these lines of business actually are, how they function, who conducts them, and whose interests they serve. The analysis shows that all of the activities examined constitute legal, economically well-founded, and in large part regulated businesses whose questionable reputation stems chiefly from opacity, conflicts of interest, and isolated excesses. Investment banking is a highly concentrated business of a few large banks, with worldwide fee income of $60.5 billion in the first half of 2025 alone. Shadow banking, as recorded by the Financial Stability Board, comprises assets of $256.8 trillion and thus already 51 per cent of the global financial system. In high-frequency trading, roughly 55 per cent of US and up to 43 per cent of European equity trading volume is attributable to strategies whose reaction times are measured in millionths of a second; the costs associated with latency arbitrage amount to roughly five billion dollars per year worldwide (Aquilina, Budish, and O'Neill, 2022). For investors, a differentiated assessment follows: none of the businesses examined is disreputable per se, and none is free of risk. Those who understand how they work, who the participants are, and where the profits originate can weigh opportunities and dangers realistically — and may, in selected cases, participate in these markets themselves, whether through listed trading firms or through regulated credit funds.

ssrn-7365822.abstract: Satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated (e.g., China's Micius satellite) as a means of extending quantum-secured communication beyond fiber-optic range, with direct relevance to naval fleet communications and aircraft-to-base communications where mobile assets cannot rely on fixed fiber infrastructure. Unlike this research group's companion terrestrial BB84 study, which evaluated eavesdropper detection under near-ideal channel conditions, satellite links are dominated by a different physical effect: atmospheric photon loss, driven by slant-path absorption, scattering, beam divergence, and elevation-angle-dependent atmospheric thickness. This study models that effect using PKTron's density-matrix simulator, explicitly separating two physically distinct phenomena that are frequently conflated in simplified models: heralded photon loss (which reduces raw key rate without directly causing bit errors) and detector dark counts (a roughly constant background click rate that becomes proportionally significant, and increasingly drives quantum bit error rate, QBER, as the real signal weakens). Across four simulated transmittance scenarios representing satellite pass geometries from zenith (η=0.50) to near-horizon (η=0.005), sifted key count fell from 547 to 15 bits per 2,000 transmitted qubits, while QBER rose from 2.6% to 33.3%, driven by dark counts constituting an increasing fraction (1.3% to 60.0%) of all detector clicks. Hardware validation was performed on IBM Quantum's ibm_marrakesh processor for the surviving-photon measurement step, using the same classical channel model to determine which photons survived transmission. At η=0.50, hardware measurement yielded a 0.550 click rate (matching theoretical prediction) with 12 sifted bits and 0.000 QBER; at η=0.03, a larger sample (400 transmitted qubits) yielded a 0.037 click rate (again matching prediction) with 8 sifted bits and a QBER of 0.125, consistent with the simulated prediction of elevated error rates at low transmittance. These results confirm, in both simulation and on real quantum hardware, that atmospheric loss degrades satellite QKD primarily through reduced key rate and a distinct, gradual, dark-count-driven QBER increase-qualitatively different from the sharp, immediate QBER signature of eavesdropping demonstrated in this group's companion terrestrial QKD study-a distinction with direct relevance to link budget engineering for naval and airborne quantum-secured communication systems.

ssrn-7366094.abstract: We provide novel evidence on how investor attention interacts with corporate disclosure during the “full-consignment” shift in cross-border e-commerce, a reversal of the decade-long platform migration toward agency selling. Using 41,236 question-and-answer dialogues from China’s regulated investor interaction platforms for 118 listed supply-chain firms over 2022–2024, we document three counterintuitive findings. Consignment-related Q&A spikes generate overpricing that is larger and reverses faster than that associated with unregulated attention proxies: a five-day abnormal return of +2.9% fully reverses within six weeks, consistent with a credibility illusion created by exchange supervision. Attention also runs backward—investor questioning induces consignment narratives, concentrated in firms that never report consignment revenue. Finally, the market rewards narrative adopters while underreacting to genuine converters. The price-formation benefits of regulated interaction platforms are thus topic-contingent, and investor questioning constitutes a novel demand-side trigger of catering disclosure.​

ssrn-7366218.abstract: We examine whether NSE index derivatives exhibit a liquidity discontinuity at 15:00 IST, tied to mandatory broker RMS auto-square-off and, historically, the 15:00-15:30 IST closing-price VWAP window. Using kernel-density clustering, regression discontinuity design, and panel GMM on real Nifty 50 (2017) and Bank Nifty (2015-2026) minute data, plus a fully re-derived 62-stock cross-section, we find significantly elevated volatility-not directional returns-at 15:00-15:15, roughly twice as large for high-retailleverage stocks. Placebo tests at nearby cutoffs are also frequently significant, indicating an accelerating volatility curve into the close rather than a sharp, uniquely localized discontinuity.

ssrn-7366638.abstract: Climate policy uncertainty has become an important consideration for strategic asset allocation, particularly for long-horizon institutional investors whose portfolios are exposed to regulatory shifts and policy reversals. This paper examines how institutional investors can translate climate policy uncertainty into implementable strategic asset-allocation rules. Motivated by the distinction between risk and Knightian ambiguity, we use climate policy uncertainty as an observable state variable that governs the strength of portfolio shrinkage. Building on this idea, we propose two allocation rules. The first is an ambiguity-penalized robust mean -variance optimizer (ARMVO), which blends the maximum-Sharpe and minimum-variance portfolios with a blending intensity controlled by the uncertainty state. The second is an ambiguity-linked Black-Litterman model (ALBL), which shrinks the expected-return input toward the reverse-optimization equilibrium return using the same state variable. We implement the two rules using a rolling percentile of the newly developed climate policy uncertainty (CPU) index of f Gavriilidis et al. (2026) and test them on eleven global ETFs from 2012 to 2024. ALBL improves the Sharpe ratio from 0.119 for equal weighting to 0.286 and generates a certainty equivalent gain of 208 basis points per year for a risk-aversion parameter of γ=5, although the Sharpe-ratio improvement is not statistically significant at conventional levels. Asset-based attribution suggests that the improvement is not fully explained by a static allocation to the same ETFs. The paper contributes a transparent and implementable framework for ambiguity-aware strategic asset allocation.

ssrn-7372261.abstract: This study examines whether pre-expiration stock liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in price reactions to a potential increase in the supply of tradable shares, using IPO lockup expirations as pre-scheduled events. We construct a hand-collected dataset of lockup contracts from IPO disclosure documents for 522 IPO firms listed on the Mothers market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange between 2012 and 2021. Because lockup expiration dates are determined at the time of the IPO, this setting mitigates concerns that event timing is chosen in response to contemporaneous market conditions. We find a negative median cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around lockup expirations, and the magnitude of the reaction varies systematically with pre-expiration liquidity. Firms with higher pre-expiration turnover experience higher CAR, and this association remains significant in the joint specification. Higher Amihud illiquidity is associated with lower CAR in separate specifications, whereas wider bid-ask spreads show a marginally significant negative association; neither association remains statistically significant in the joint specification. The liquidity–CAR association is concentrated in the post-expiration window and is not statistically significant in the pre-expiration window, consistent with variation in post-expiration price reactions rather than pre-existing return trends. Overall, pre-expiration liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in post-expiration price reactions, with the most robust evidence coming from turnover.

ssrn-7372321.abstract: This study analyses whether gold acts as a hedge or safe haven for the Indian stock market using long-run and crisis-specific return-based methods. Monthly data from 2008–2025 and daily data for the Global Financial Crisis, COVID-19, and the Russia–Ukraine war are used to estimate Pearson and Spearman correlations between gold and Nifty returns, with 60, 120, and 240-day windows. Results show moderate negative long-run correlation, indicating partial hedging, while safe-haven behaviour varies across crises and is strongest during the Russia–Ukraine war, highlighting time-varying diversification benefits.

ssrn-7372430.abstract: This paper evaluates the extent to which standard quantitative sovereign default models exhibit equity return responses around default risk spikes comparable to the data. It finds that they largely do not. Hébert and Schreger (2017) employ a high-frequency event study around legal rulings and report a 10% increase in default risk causes a 6% decline in firms’ market value. A workhorse sovereign default model augmented with capital accumulation delivers only a 0.2% equity value drop. Three features account for the disconnect: the absence of private capital outflows and trade surpluses during default, the model’s counterfactual prediction of rising dividends, and the nominal depreciation embedded in the dollar-denominated index used in the data.

ssrn-7375459.abstract: Retail investors reveal in public which stocks they are crowding into, and those stocks become more volatile the following week. Option prices, the market's forecast of that volatility, absorb only about half the signal. Measured from 86.7 million Reddit comments, attention keeps half its predictive power after the full surface is observed, and nonlinear readings do not close the gap. The absorbed half runs through the at-the-money term structure, not the smile, which attention nonetheless reshapes. The unabsorbed half improves volatility forecasts out of sample. Controlling for implied volatility does not control for what retail attention predicts.

ssrn-7375459.title: Half the Signal: Retail Attention and the Price of Volatility

ssrn-7375498.abstract: This paper investigates whether unsupervised machine learning can identify economically meaningful regimes in the US equity market and whether such regimes provide genuine forecasting or investment value. Using a daily dataset of 3,823 observations spanning 18 October 2010 to 31 December 2025, sixteen standardized market, volatility, and macro-financial features are reduced via Principal Component Analysis (eight components explaining 92.1% of variance) and partitioned using K-Means clustering, validated against a Gaussian Mixture Model. The optimal solution, selected by silhouette score, identifies two statistically and economically distinct regimes, subsequently labelled Bull / Low-Risk (n = 3,201; 83.7% of observations) and Bear / High-Risk (n = 622; 16.3%). The regimes differ significantly across mean return, volatility, VIX level, momentum, and drawdown (Welch t-tests, all p < .001; Cohen's d up to 2.94), and exhibit strong persistence, with Bull-to-Bull and Bear-to-Bear transition probabilities of 96.5% and 81.8% respectively. A chronological, one-step-ahead out-of-sample forecasting exercise compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting classifiers against a naive persistence benchmark ("tomorrow's regime equals today's regime"). The persistence benchmark achieved the highest out-of-sample accuracy (93.55%), exceeding Random Forest (91.89%), Logistic Regression (89.80%), and Gradient Boosting (89.01%). This finding does not support the hypothesis that supervised machine learning provides superior next-day regime forecasting relative to a simple persistence rule. A regime-conditioned tactical investment strategy (fully invested in Bull, fully divested in Bear, signal lagged by one day, 10 basis point transaction costs) reduced maximum drawdown relative to buy-and-hold (-28.20% versus-33.92%) but underperformed on both compound annual growth rate (5.80% versus 12.68%) and Sharpe ratio (0.546 versus 0.780). Forward-return analysis indicates that returns following Bear/High-Risk observations were, on average, higher than returns following Bull/Low-Risk observations at 1-, 5-, and 20-day horizons, offering a plausible explanation for the strategy's return shortfall despite its lower drawdown. The study concludes that regime identification is statistically robust and economically interpretable, but that regime identification is not equivalent to reliable regime forecasting or to superior risk-adjusted investment performance. The paper's contribution lies in this explicit separation of unsupervised classification, supervised forecasting, and economic usefulness-three distinct questions that are frequently conflated in applied machine learning finance research. A supplementary robustness check (Section XI.J), which widens the feature set to twenty-nine variables by restoring the raw price, volume, and moving-average series the main specification deliberately excludes, produces a weaker four-regime solution and a severe train/test distribution shift that collapses out-of-sample forecasting performance-a negative result that, if anything, reinforces the original feature-exclusion rationale in Section IV.

summary.takeaway: 국면 분류는 리스크 대시보드나 포지션 사이징 보조 지표로만 쓰고, 다음날 국면 예측 모델을 새로 얹는 대신 '오늘 국면 유지' 규칙을 기준선으로 삼는다

ssrn-7375618.abstract: A fund can look greener without its manager shifting the portfolio toward greener firms. Independent measures agree that U.S. mutual fund carbon intensity fell by more than a third, yet portfolio reweighting explains only 1.2 percent. Most of the decline instead comes from changing issuer emissions, sales denominators, estimates, and coverage. These inputs reverse the institutional sector trend and reshuffle manager rankings. Attribution replaces two in five managers selected for a green mandate. The replacements subsequently trade greener than those they displace. Carbon scores measure portfolio exposure; attribution reveals who deserves credit for changing it.

ssrn-7375738.abstract: Passive inflows do not make firms issue equity indiscriminately. They redirect corporate share supply toward firms with real opportunities. I isolate those opportunities using federal purchasing growth in markets served by a firm's customers, which raises the firm's own sales. Index funds mostly get their shares from compensation and other transactions that bring the firm no money, and inflows raise no offerings on average. When a real opportunity arrives, supply shifts toward primary shares that raise cash. Firms already indexed issue far less against the same opportunity. Indexed ownership decides which opportunities get financed with new equity.

summary.relevance_why: 지수 보유 지분과 발행 유형은 표준 데이터로 얻지만, 고객사 시장별 연방 조달 자료는 산업 연결과 수작업 매칭이 필요해 확보 난이도가 높다
